topic: Small oscillations of spring-linked equal pendulums
problem: Two mathematical pendulums each with a length l are connected by a weightless spring as shown in Fig. 228. The coefficient of elasticity of the spring is k. In equilibrium the pendulums occupy a vertical position and the spring is not deformed. Determine the frequencies of small oscillations of the two linked pendulums when they are deflected in one plane through equal angles in one direction (oscillations in phase) and in opposite directions (oscillations in antiphase).

image_derived_facts: Two equal bob masses: both bobs bear the label m.
Two distinct fixed suspension points on a common support; each vertical pendulum is labelled l.
The horizontal spring connects the bobs directly at the equilibrium bob level.
problem_figure.policy: The actual user-provided image was inspected directly. These provenance notes are extracted observations, not a trusted-caption intermediary.

source_text_facts: Two mathematical pendulums of equal length l.
Small planar in-phase and antiphase equal-angle motions.
solution: In phase the spring does not change length, giving angular frequency ω_in=√(g/l). In antiphase the supplied explanation uses spring force 2kl sin φ and restoring force Fr=mg sin φ+2kl sin φ cos φ. With cos φ approximately 1 in the small-angle regime it obtains ω_anti=√((g+2kl/m)/l)=√(g/l+2k/m).

solution_figure.note: The task describes displaced-pendulum force annotations. No separate Fig. 479 image file was identified or used; the provided solution text guides the audit. Neither force annotations nor final formulas are original-image premises.

formal_interpretation: Ask for unique positive angular-frequency witnesses satisfying both bob rotational equations with the equilibrium derivative of the exact symmetric-mode torques. Candidate derives signed spring extension, tangential projection, torque derivatives and both formulas from upstream SimplePendulum and HarmonicOscillator. The exact tangent-linear model is adopted for small oscillations; no finite-angle trigonometric approximation is made into an equality.

modeling_choices: Positive l,m,k,g and pivot separation; no numerical source values.
Gravity g and pivot separation parameterize the ideal model; separation is not a printed source label.
Ideal point bobs, weightless rigid-length links and massless Hooke spring; no damping.
Linearized dynamics is defined by the derivative of mode-slice torque at vertical equilibrium.
Angular frequencies use radians per unit time, not cyclic frequencies in Hz.
